title: Senate Confirms Brett Matsumoto as BLS Commissioner, Ending Year-Long Vacancy
detail: The Senate confirmed career economist Brett Matsumoto as commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics on August 7, 2026, in a 51-47 vote covering a block of nominees. The role had been vacant since President Trump abruptly fired commissioner Erika McEntarfer in August 2025 over a weak July 2025 jobs report, and after Trump's initial pick, Heritage Foundation economist E.J. Antoni, was withdrawn amid Republican opposition. Matsumoto, who holds a Ph.D. in economics from UNC Chapel Hill, joined BLS in 2015 as an inflation expert and was on leave at the White House Council of Economic Advisers when selected. He will serve a four-year term overseeing US jobs and inflation data.

media.caption: Senate confirms Brett Matsumoto as BLS commissioner after year-long vacancy
